toward altruistic behavior in people, so look for and highlight clues in the passage about that

day. A good word for the blank to enter in the annotation box would be “diminish” or “reduce.”

more curiosity about the outcome of a video were less
likely, not more likely as expected by researchers, to
use a provided ‘spoiler’ button to skip to the video’s
conclusion than were subjects reporting indifference

thwarting it.

rw.exp:
This is a Vocabulary question, as it asks for a logical and precise word or phrase to fill in the blank. The 
blank should describe the findings of the study, so look for and highlight clues in the passage about 
those findings. Highlight that subjects expressing more curiosity about the outcome of a video were less 
likely, not more likely as expected by researchers to do something. Note also the contrast expressed by 
Hsiung at the end of the text. A good word for the blank to enter in the annotation box would be 
“contradictory” or “unexpected.”
	
	
	
• 
(A) is wrong because unprecedented is Extreme Language—there’s not enough evidence in the 
passage to claim that no other study had ever found results like these before.
	
	
	
• 
(B) is wrong because ambivalent is Recycled Language—it misuses indifference from the 
passage, which is used only to describe the attitude of some of the subjects.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is correct because paradoxical matches “contradictory.”
	
	
	
• 
(D) is wrong because vague does not match “contradictory.”

Etty Bachar-Wikström was inspired by reports of the
remarkable ability of sharks to heal from wounds
sustained in the wild. Despite previous data suggesting
that chemicals found in shark skin may have significant
biomedical potential, researchers before Wikström and
Bachar-Wikström had not ________ the comprehensive
and numerous experiments necessary to explore this
phenomenon in controlled laboratory conditions.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical
and precise word or phrase?
rw.exp:
This is a Vocabulary question, as it asks for a logical and precise word or phrase to fill in the blank. The 
blank should describe the interaction between the researchers before Wikström and Bachar-Wikström 
and comprehensive and numerous experiments, so look for and highlight clues in the passage about this 
interaction. Highlight that the previous data suggested that chemicals found in shark skin may have 
significant biomedical potential. The transition word Despite introduces a contrast—though you’d

•

The following text is adapted from James Weldon’s 1912
book. In the text, Johnson discusses the skilled workers
of the cigar-making trade.
He was able to make a bundle of one hundred cigars
in a day, not one of which could be told from the
others by any difference in size or shape, or even by
any appreciable difference in weight. This was the
acme of artistic skill in cigar making. Workmen of
this class were rare, never more than three or four in
one factory, and it was never necessary for them to
remain out of work. There were men who made two,
three, and four hundred cigars of the cheaper grades
in a day; they had to be very fast in order to make a
decent week’s wages.
Which choice best describes the function of the
underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

opts.text: It emphasizes the competence with which the cigar-maker engages in his daily work.
It compares the technique of cigar-making to the craft of making a piece of art.
It suggests that the more skilled workers do not make the cheaper cigars.
It shows how the workmen are affected by the conditions of the cigar factory. |

rw.exp:
This is a Purpose question, as it asks for the function of the underlined sentence in the passage. Read 
the passage and highlight clues in the sentence before and after that can help understand the function 
of the underlined sentence. The word This in the underlined sentence indicates the sentence before, 
which states that He was able to make a bundle of one hundred cigars in a day, not one of which could be 
told from the others by any difference in size or shape. The underlined sentence calls this consistency the 
acme of artistic skill in cigar making.  Therefore, a good function of the underlined sentence to enter in 
the annotation box would be “claim that the cigar maker is highly skilled.”
	
	
	
• 
(A) is correct because it’s consistent with the highlighting and annotation.
	
	
	
• 
(B) is wrong because it contains Recycled Language—it misuses the reference to artistic skill 
from the passage to make a claim about a piece of art.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is wrong because it’s Right Answer, Wrong Question—only the last sentence, not the 
underlined sentence, introduces the cheaper cigars. Furthermore, it’s not clear from the passage 
that the men who make the cheaper cigars are definitely less skilled than the man from the 
opening sentences, just that they had to be very fast.
	
	
	
• 
(D) is wrong because it goes Beyond the Text—as easy as it is to imagine the conditions of a 
factory affecting the workmen, no such description is given in the passage.

The following text is from Charles Dickens’s 1861 novel
Great Expectations. Pip, the narrator, has just gained a
considerable fortune from an anonymous benefactor.
I took it upon myself to impress Biddy (and through
Biddy, Joe) with the grave obligation I considered
my friends under, to know nothing and say nothing
about the maker of my fortune. It would all come
out in good time, I observed, and in the meanwhile
nothing was to be said, save that I had come into great
expectations from a mysterious patron.
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

opts.text: To explain that Pip finds his new fortune both stressful and immensely rejuvenating
To describe Pip’s resolve to not discuss the identity of his benefactor
To detail a conflict between Pip’s internal excitement and external confidence
To highlight Pip’s desire to impress his friends with his newfound wealth 4 | Harder Reading and Writing Module

rw.exp:
This is a Purpose question, as it asks for the main purpose of the text. Read the passage and highlight 
clues that can help understand the main purpose. Highlight that Pip wanted his friends to know 
nothing and say nothing about the maker of my fortune and that nothing was to be said.  Therefore, a 
good main purpose to enter in the annotation box would be “explain that Pip doesn’t want identity 
of his patron talked about.”
	
	
	
• 
(A) is wrong because it goes Beyond the Text—both of these emotions could be connected to 
gaining a large sum of money, but neither is expressed by Pip in the passage.
	
	
	
• 
(B) is correct because it’s consistent with the highlighting and annotation—Pip believes the 
information will all come out in good time, so he does not want to discuss the identity of his 
benefactor now.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is wrong because it’s Half-Right—while the passage does seem to suggest some confident 
on Pip’s part, as he believes all the information about his benefactor will come out in good time, 
there is nothing that could be internal excitement in the passage.
	
	
	
• 
(D) is wrong because it contains Recycled Language—it misuses impress and friends from the 
first sentence to generate an unsupported desire of Pip’s.

works, incorporates natural processes and innovative
approaches to his artistic methods. In 2008, he created
a series of works under the project name Crystallized,
which involved using water tanks containing a special
solution to grow natural crystals. During the growth
process, the solution was exposed to the continuous
pulsations of a specific musical piece, such as “Swan

the resulting crystalline shape. Although the finished
work appears sculptural, Tokujin refers to these pieces
as “crystallized paintings,” suggesting that just as the

emotional experience.

text?

opts.text: It discusses Tokujin’s work in detail, then draws a conclusion about Tokujin’s artistic history.
It introduces an artist’s general approach, then describes a specific instance of that approach.
It contrasts the crystallized painting derived from “Swan Lake” with the one derived from “Moonlight.”
It describes Tokujin’s approach, then explains how the music of “Swan Lake” influenced his work.

rw.exp:
This is a Purpose question, as it asks for the overall structure of the text. Read the passage and highlight 
connections between ideas to understand the overall structure. Highlight that Yoshioka Tokujin 
incorporates natural processes and innovative approaches to his artistic methods. Immediately after, 
the phrase In 2008 introduces an example of this: the Crystallized project. The rest of the passage 
describes this project and some of Tokujin’s thoughts on it. Therefore, a good overall structure to 
enter in the annotation box would be “explain Tokujin’s work and give an example of the work.”
	
	
	
• 
(A) is wrong because it’s Half-Right—the passage does discuss Tokujin’s work in detail, but his 
history as an artist is not given.
	
	
	
• 
(B) is correct because it’s consistent with the highlighting and annotation.
	
	
	
• 
(C) and (D) are wrong because they both contain Recycled Language—“Swan Lake” and 
“Moonlight” are mentioned in the passage but not contrasted with each other, nor does the 
passage claim that the music of “Swan Lake” influenced Tokujin, just that “Swan Lake” is a 
musical piece.

rw.stem:
Text 1
The origin of mitochondria has long been assumed to
be a single-celled prokaryote swallowing a bacterium,
forming a eukaryote. But when a group of scientists led
by Toni Gabaldón started sequencing modern genomes,
they found evidence of more than two “partners”
in the original synthesis. Gabaldón and his team
hypothesize that these simple cellular ancestors shared
genetic material via a variety of partners that led to
the development of eukaryotes in a more “horizontal,”
or branching, fashion. This discovery may lead to the
rewriting of our narrative of how our genes evolved.
Text 2
While Gabaldón and colleagues advocate for a
“gradual” evolution of cell symbionts involving
multiple genetic partners, it’s too soon to recast the
beginnings of mitochondria. For the cells to employ
such a multidirectional evolutionary pathway, they
would more likely already have been more complex
eukaryotic cells, not simple prokaryotes. Gabaldón’s
observations of modern host eukaryotes may therefore
not reveal as much about the behavior of ancestral
prokaryotes as originally believed.
Based on the texts, what would the author of Text 2 say
about Gabaldón and his team’s hypothesis regarding
the evidence found in Text 1?

opts.text: It is understandable given that the gene sequencing performed by Gabaldón is the first use of this groundbreaking technology.
It is surprising given that the traditional assumptions of the origin of the mitochondria contradict Gabaldón’s theory.
It may not accurately depict the nature of the organism involved in the evolutionary process described by the theory.
It is overly simplistic given the complexity of the genome sequencing performed by Gabaldón. |

rw.exp:
This is a Dual Texts question, as it asks what the author of Text 2 would say about Gabaldón and his 
team’s hypothesis from Text 1. Read Text 1 and highlight the hypothesis, which is that these simple 
cellular ancestors shared genetic material via a variety of partners that led to the development of eukaryotes 
in a more “horizontal,” or branching, fashion. Then, read Text 2 and highlight what its author says 
about the same topic: Gabaldón’s observations of modern host eukaryotes may therefore not reveal as 
much about the behavior of ancestral prokaryotes as originally believed. Therefore, the author of Text 2 
believes that eukaryotes would need to have formed before, not after, the type of evolution described 
by Gabaldón and his team. Enter “Text 2 disagrees—G’s hypothesis does not provide answer” into 
the annotation box. 
	
	
	
• 
(A) is wrong because it’s Extreme Language—it’s not known that Gabaldón and his team 
are the first to use gene sequencing technology or that it’s considered groundbreaking by either 
author. Additionally, understandable would not capture the disagreement between the passages.

• 
(B) is wrong because it’s Half-Right—while Gabaldón and his team’s theory is indeed 
contradictory to the traditional assumption regarding mitochondria in Text 1, the author 
of Text 2 does not cite this contrast, focusing instead on the type of evolution suggested by 
Gabaldón and his team.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is correct because it’s consistent with the highlighting and annotated relationship between 
the passages—the author of Text 2 believes that eukaryotes, not prokaryotes, are the organisms 
capable of the type of evolution discussed in Text 1.
	
	
	
• 
(D) is wrong because it’s not the genome sequencing that the author of Text 2 takes issue 
with—it’s the complexity of the organism required to participate in the type of evolution that 
Gabaldón suggests.

Recently discovered in China, Proterocladus antique is
the scientific name for an algae fossil approximately
a billion years old. Using samples from the well-
preserved Nanfen formation (an ancient seabed), Qing
Tang, Ke Pang, Xunlai Yuan and Shuhai Xiao found
that P. antique was a green alga that could, like its
modern relative seaweed, photosynthesize—that is,
manufacture sugars and oxygen from light and carbon
dioxide. Tang maintains that P. antique indicates that
green algae first evolved in the oceans instead of in
freshwater environments such as lakes and rivers.
Which of the following, if true, would most directly
support Tang’s claim?

opts.text: The fossils are visible to the naked eye, which indicates that P. antique was one of the largest creatures of the era, sharing the seas with smaller organisms such as bacteria.
The fossils of P. antique are evenly distributed in the Nanfen formation with fossils of freshwater algae and other photosynthesizing organisms from the same era.

Green algae such as P. antique and sea lettuce do the majority of photosynthesis on the planet, while land plants, which evolved later, are responsible for a less substantial proportion of the process.
The oldest scientifically legitimized fossil of green algae from a freshwater environment is confirmed to be only about 800 million years old.

rw.exp:
This is a Claims question, as it asks which choice would most directly support Tang’s claim. Look for 
and highlight the claim in the passage, which is that green algae first evolved in the oceans instead of in 
freshwater environments such as lakes and rivers. Note that this claim is based on the one-billion-year-
old fossil Proterocladus antique. The correct answer should be as consistent as possible with this claim 
and its evidence.
	
	
	
• 
(A) and (C) are wrong because they’re both irrelevant to the claim—the size of the fossils and 
the comparison of the roles of Green algae and sea lettuce to that of land plants would not affect 
whether or not green algae first evolved in the oceans rather than in freshwater environments.
	
	
	
• 
(B) is wrong because if anything, it would weaken or confuse Tang’s claim if the fossils of P. 
antique were found in the Nanfen formation with freshwater algae, as Tang is using the fact 
that the Nanfen formation is an ancient seabed as part of his evidence for why green algae first 
evolved in the oceans rather than in freshwater environments.
	
	
	
• 
(D) is correct because if the oldest fossil of green algae from a freshwater environment was only 
about 800 million years old, the P. antique fossil would be older by about 200 million years. This 
would support the claim that green algae developed in the oceans first.

Mineralogists are often asked to determine whether
certain impact events are caused by asteroids
(comprised of metals and rock) or fragments of comets
(comprised of ice, dust, and rock). In 1927, Soviet
mineralogist Leonid Kulik concluded that one of the
Earth’s major impacts, the 1908 Tunguska event,
occurred when an asteroid exploded a few miles above
the ground. According to Kulik, his conclusion was
supported by the fact that though the impact flattened
miles of forest, it left no crater, which suggests that the
object primarily collided with the Earth’s atmosphere
rather than the surface.
Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken
Kulik’s conclusion?

opts.text: Researchers tested material from tree cores within the zone of impact, and found high levels of material rarely found in comets but frequently found in rocky asteroids.
A comet fragment would have disintegrated before reaching the lower atmosphere, but the Tunguska event object stayed intact through most of the lower atmosphere.
As the celestial body that caused the Tunguska event passed through the atmosphere, such pressures and temperatures developed that the object abruptly exploded.
After the event, researchers and locals searched for metal-laced rock fragments over the area of impact, but no such objects were ever reported discovered. |

rw.exp:
This is a Claims question, as it asks which choice would most directly weaken Kulik’s conclusion. Look 
for and highlight the conclusion in the passage, which is that one of the Earth’s major impacts, the 1908 
Tunguska event, occurred when an asteroid exploded a few miles above the ground. Note also the additional 
support given to this claim in the last sentence and the features of asteroids from the first sentence. The 
correct answer should be as consistent as possible with this conclusion and its associated details.
	
	
	
• 
(A) and (B) are wrong because, if anything, they would strengthen Kulik’s claim by making it 
more likely that the object was an asteroid rather than a comet.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is wrong because it’s irrelevant to the claim—the circumstances that caused the explosion of 
the object don’t contribute positively or negatively to whether the object was an asteroid or not.
	
	
	
• 
(D) is correct because it’s consistent with the question task and detail from the passage—
asteroids are said to be comprised of metals and rock. If no such metal or rock-based fragments 
were ever reported discovered near the area of impact, this may reduce the likelihood that an 
asteroid was responsible for the impact.

Following a prolific career producing paintings and
mixed media art centered around her Native American
heritage and focused on socio-political commentary,
Jaune Quick-to-See Smith became the first Native
American painter whose work has appeared in the
National Gallery of Art. According to an Associated
Press journalist, Smith was shocked that her “I See
Red: Target” was the first painting on canvas done
by a Native American artist to enter the museum’s
collection, although the journalist went on to clarify
that the museum had previously featured Indigenous
works in other forms of media.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support the
journalist’s clarification?

opts.text: Smith’s work has been widely exhibited across prominent museums such as the Museum of Modern Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the National Museum of Women in the Arts, and the Smithsonian American Art Museum.

Smith has not only had her work displayed in multiple prominent exhibits, but she has also collaborated on public art displays including the floor design in the Great Hall of the Denver Airport and a mile-long history trail in West Seattle.

A spokeswoman for the National Gallery of Art comments in an interview that the museum has over two dozen works on paper by Indigenous authors and that the gallery is excited to add a painting to its collection of Native American art.

Since the museum acquired Smith’s work, Smith has brought together art by other Native American artists to showcase contemporary works of art by Native Americans that reflect the diversity among their regional, cultural, and individual identities as well as a shared worldview of mutual reverence and concern for the land. 8 | Harder Reading and Writing Module

rw.exp:
This is a Claims question, as it asks which choice would most directly support the journalist’s 
clarification. Look for and highlight the clarification in the passage, which is that the museum has 
previously featured Indigenous works in other forms of media. Note that this clarification is in response 
to Smith being shocked that hers was the first painting on canvas done by a Native American artist 
to enter the museum’s collection. The correct answer should be as consistent as possible with the 
clarification and its relation to Smith’s reaction.
	
	
	
• 
(A) and (B) are wrong because they’re both irrelevant to the claim—both of these answers focus 
on other venues or areas that have exhibited Smith’s work rather than specifically address the 
collection of Indigenous works by the National Gallery of Art.
	
	
	
• 
(C) is correct because it’s consistent with both the journalist’s clarification that the museum has 
Indigenous works in other forms of media and confirms that Smith’s was indeed the first Native 
American artist’s painting on canvas to be added to the collection.

• 
(D) is wrong because it goes Beyond the Text—as reasonable a course of action as this would be 
for Smith, seeing as she may think Native American art to be underrepresented, the journalist’s 
clarification does not address Smith’s actions after being shocked.

In the given system of equations, k is a constant.
When the equations are graphed in the xy-plane, they
intersect only once at the point with coordinates (x, y).

math.exp:
The question asks for a value in a system of equations. Enter both equations into the built-in 
calculator, and click on the slider tool for k. Move the slider back and forth until the line intersects 
the parabola only once. This may take some fine-tuning and some scrolling and zooming to see when 
there is one point of intersection, which occurs when k = 5. Click on the gray dot to see that the 
coordinates are (1, –1). The question asks for the value of y, which is –1. Note that the value of x, 1, 
and the value of k, 5, are both answer choices. RTFQ to get (B) as the correct answer.
	
	
	
It is also possible to solve algebraically, although it takes longer. The given equations are both equal 
to y, so set them equal to each other. The new equation becomes –3x2 + 10x – 8 = 4x – k. Subtract 4x 
from both sides of the equation to get –3x2 + 6x – 8 = – k; then add k to both sides of the equation to 
get –3x2 + 6x – 8 + k = 0.
	
	
	
The question states that the graphs of the equations intersect only once, so use the discriminant. The 
discriminant is the part of the quadratic formula under the square root sign, and it can be written 
as D = b2 – 4ac. When the discriminant is positive, the quadratic has exactly two real solutions; 
when the discriminant is 0, the quadratic has exactly one real solution; and when the discriminant is 
negative, the quadratic has no real solutions. In this case, the quadratic has exactly one real solution, 
so the discriminant must equal 0.
	
	
	
With the equation in standard form, a = –3, b = 6, and c = –8 + k. Plug these values into the 
discriminant formula and set it equal to 0 to get (6)2 – 4(–3)(–8 + k) = 0. Simplify the left side of 
the equation to get 36 + 12(–8 + k) = 0. Distribute the 12 to get 36 – 96 + 12k = 0. Simplify further 
to get –60 + 12k = 0; then add 60 to both sides of the equation to get 12k = 60. Finally, divide both 
sides of the equation by 12 to get k = 5.
	
	
	
Read carefully: the question asks for the value of y, not the value of k. Eliminate (D), which is likely 
a trap because it is the value of k. Plug k = 5 into the first equation to get y = 4x – 5. Enter both 
equations into the built-in calculator; then scroll and zoom as needed to see that the graphs intersect 
at the point (1, –1). The question asks for the value of y, which is –1.
	
	
	
Using either method, the correct answer is (B).
